dossier.public_summary: The 11.3-day dips alternate between about 1,600 ppm and 5,000 ppm, so odd and even events differ by a factor of three, as seen in all three sectors. A single transit is even much deeper and the transit-to-transit depths are statistically inconsistent. That is best explained by a stellar companion eclipsing a similar or slightly different star every 22.6 days, not a 2.7-Earth-radius planet on the target.

reasons.why: Odd and even eclipses differ at high significance with depth ratio ~3.3 and all sectors same sign, as expected for a binary at twice the 11.3 d period (22.6 d), not spot variability.
